meta.title: K-Bap — read any Korean menu
meta.description: Point your camera at a Korean menu. K-Bap translates every dish and marks the ones containing ingredients you listed as off-limits.
hero.headline: You can't read the menu. K-Bap can.
hero.sub: Point your camera at a Korean menu. Every dish comes back in your language, and the ones containing ingredients from your avoid list are marked.
hero.note: Free. Browse as a guest, or sign up to have dishes rated against your own list.
hero.shotAlt: The K-Bap home screen, with a scan button and dishes rated safe for the user
problem.title: Korean menus give you names and prices, rarely ingredients.
problem.body: You know what you can't eat, and the menu gives you no way to check. K-Bap reads the Korean and checks each dish against the ingredients you listed.
features.title: Eight things you get
f1.title: Scan a menu
f1.body: One photo of a Korean menu. K-Bap reads the Korean, gives you each dish in your language, and rates it against the ingredients you avoid.
f1.alt: The K-Bap home screen with a Scan a menu button and a row of dishes rated safe
f2.title: 81 ingredients to pick from
f2.body: Tap what you skip, from peanut and butter to alcohol and shellfish. Fifteen presets, among them vegan, halal, kosher and gluten-free, fill the list in for you, and you can edit any entry afterwards.
f2.alt: The edit restrictions screen with egg, butter and peanut selected from a grid of ingredient chips
f3.title: A rating built from your list
f3.body: Every dish carries one of four labels, worked out from the list you saved. Change the list and the ratings change with it.
f3.alt: A dish detail screen showing an Avoid for you label and the ingredients behind it
f4.title: Browse without scanning
f4.body: Search Korean dishes by name or scroll the catalog. Each card carries the same rating a scanned dish would get.
f4.alt: A grid of Korean dishes, each with a risk badge in the corner
f5.title: See which ingredient caused it
f5.body: Open a dish and its ingredients come back in risk order, each one labeled and marked with how often restaurants use it. Spice level sits at the top, on a scale of ten.
f5.alt: The What's inside panel listing butter as an ingredient to avoid, found in about 60 percent of restaurants
f6.title: Ask in Korean without speaking it
f6.body: K-Bap writes the question, or the whole order, in Korean. Show the staff the screen and they read what you can't eat.
f6.alt: A card written in Korean asking whether the dish contains butter, to show restaurant staff
f6.alt2: A Korean order card that asks for one dish and lists the ingredients the diner can't eat
f7.title: Reviews from other diners
f7.body: Read what other people made of a dish before you order it, and add your own once you've tried it.
f8.title: My Foods
f8.body: Two lists on your profile: what you ordered and what you scanned. Useful when you want that dish again and can't remember the name.
risk.title: The four labels
risk.sub: Color alone is easy to miss, so each label carries its own shape.
risk.safe.label: Safe
risk.safe.body: Nothing from your avoid list turned up in this dish.
risk.caution.label: Caution
risk.caution.body: Recipes differ between restaurants, so ask before you order.
risk.avoid.label: Avoid
risk.avoid.body: This dish contains something you listed as off-limits.
risk.nodata.label: No data
risk.nodata.body: We can't rate this dish yet. Don't read that as safe. Ask the restaurant.
langs.title: Read the menu in your own language
langs.sub: Dish names, ingredients and descriptions come back in whichever of these you pick.
cta.title: Get K-Bap before your next meal in Korea
float.label: Install K-Bap
footer.disclaimer: Ingredient information is a guide, not medical advice. Always confirm with the restaurant.
